newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Dollar resumes slide against Colombian peso.
newsitem.headline: Dollar resumes slide against Colombian peso.

text.p: The dollar slide picked up where it left off last week, falling a further 1.35 percent against the Colombian peso to end Monday's session at 1,009.25 pesos -- its lowest level since January 12.
"Trading was quite thin today. Industry was placing dollars in the market, but not in any great volumes. Demand too was very sluggish," one interbank trader said.

Potential buyers are holding off for the time being because they believe the dollar rate will continue falling, traders said. Future movements in the dollar-peso rate are unclear and nobody is betting how far the dollar may fall.
"The worst thing is that the Central Bank is not going to step in because a strengthening peso is the only way of controlling inflation that took off again in September," one trader said.
Colombia's inflation figure for the year to date hit 18.43 percent in September, topping the 17 percent originally forecast for 1996.

Dealers recorded 234 trades totaling $79.2 million. The peso opened at 1,009.05, hit an intraday high of 1,012 pesos per dollar and sank to a low of 1,009. -- Juan Guillermo Londoo, Bogota newsroom, 571 6107544
